assessments.reasoning: The cover and February 1966 preface bind CPB-441A. Section A explicitly names the language offered by the General Electric time-sharing service. Sections C and D describe language-facing input and data declarations.

challenge.method: Compare the GE-235 catalog heading with the GE-265 manual cover and contemporaneous system description. Contrast the older Dartmouth memo and the 1962 LGP-30 material.
challenge.results: GE’s systems manual identifies the GE-235 computer as part of the GE-265 system. The 1964 memo revised in 1965 describes an unfinished compiler. The earlier LGP-30 documents define a distinct machine-system scope.

limitations: This finding names the documented February 1966 service language, not a claimed single compiler lineage across all Dartmouth projects.
